title: Russia, Ukraine engage in 4-hour session on first day of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
summary: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington made another push to end the war that followed Moscow's all-out invasion of its…

image.caption: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, right, speaks as his colleague Jared Kushner, left, and NATO official Alexus Grynkewich listen, at the beginning of talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates on Tuesday. (Altaf Qadri/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·Updated

Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington made another push to end the war that followed Moscow's all-out invasion of its neighbour nearly five years ago.
Warring sides say they want peace as U.S. pushes for a resolution to the war that began in February 2022

The first day of talks in Abu Dhabi concluded after nearly four hours, the RIA Novosti news agency said. They are expected to resume on Wednesday, according to the press office of the Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine.
There are no signs the fighting is abating, and the talks took place against a backdrop of new long-range strikes between Russia and Ukraine. The two armies are largely deadlocked on the front line.
Russia launched 162 drones of various types and a ballistic missile at Ukraine overnight, Ukraine's air force said.
Russia attacked 10 ‌Ukrainian regions overnight, hitting ​five major ​energy substations that ​transmit electricity between ⁠regions, ⁠Ukrainian ‌Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi ⁠said on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Russia's Ministry of Defence said that its forces shot down 155 Ukrainian drones overnight above eight Russian regions, as well as the Crimean Peninsula, which Russia annexed from Ukraine in 2014.
Firefighters work at the site of a residential building hit by a Russian jet drone strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, on Tuesday. (Reuters)

The U.S. is renewing a push to end the war between Moscow and Kyiv after three rounds of negotiations earlier this year. The conflict, Europe's biggest since the Second World War, began after Russia's all-out invasion on Feb. 24, 2022.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the talks "constructive and quite substantive" and said they had included humanitarian and security issues.

blocks.text: "The release of prisoners [of war] is a priority. They spoke in detail about the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine and the foundations for ensuring these guarantees function over the long term," he posted on X.
Security guarantees also were discussed, he added during an appearance at the University of Copenhagen in Denmark.
European diplomats meet with U.S. envoys

U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner who, along with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, is trying to broker a settlement, said he believed there were "some good ideas how to bridge" the differences between the two sides.

Trump, whose stance on the war has varied, with more frequent criticisms of Kyiv than the Kremlin in recent weeks, must reckon with Democrats taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections. Democrats could demand more support for Ukraine.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in an interview with ZDF television on Monday night that he didn't have "overly high expectations" from the talks.
How involved is Melania Trump in the push for peace in Ukraine?
NATO commander U.S. Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, who was also present at the talks, pointed to "some great progress in the past in a military-to-military dialogue in a trilateral format."
Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service who leads Kyiv's delegation, thanked the U.S. for its efforts to end Russia's invasion.
"Our people are waiting to end this war. And we hope that we will achieve the lasting peace for Ukraine," he said.

blocks.text: Umerov said the day began with a meeting between the Ukrainian team, the U.S. envoys and representatives from the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, NATO and the European Commission.
Russia has objected to the Europeans' involvement in the three-way talks but said EU representatives could join at a later stage.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, expressed hope the meeting "will allow us to advance on the path towards peace in the interests of the people of Russia and the people of Ukraine."

Russia and Ukraine hold to their divergent demands
The Russian and Ukrainian governments remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal to end the full-scale war, now nearing its five-year mark.

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.
This is how residents of the besieged town of Oleshky stayed alive

Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that it would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.

Zelenskyy rejects Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia hasn't been able to take on the battlefield. Zelenskyy also rejects any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.

Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in Moscow, said Tuesday that it would be wiser to discuss ⁠the outlines of the future security ‌architecture in Europe first, and then a ​ceasefire in Ukraine.

blocks.text: While the ground battles have morphed into a war of attrition along the 1,200-kilometre front line, Russia and Ukraine have ramped up their long-range strikes with drones and missiles.

Russia has intensified its air campaign against Ukraine's power grid, seeking to weaken the country's resolve as winter sets in. Moscow has relied on ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, taking advantage of Ukraine's shortage of U.S.-made Patriot interceptors.
Ukraine, meanwhile, has escalated its drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
